newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish interest rates to decline sharply in '97 - NCB.
newsitem.headline: Irish interest rates to decline sharply in '97 - NCB.

text.p: Irish money market rates and bond yields are set to decline sharply this year, one of Ireland's leading firms of stockbrokers said on Wednesday.
Economic and monetary union should begin on schedule with Ireland among its founder members, said NCB Stockbrokers, adding that it expected the single currency to push rates lower.
It noted that the Irish pound was at the top of a very stretched ERM band which "absolutely precludes any further increase in interest rates".
"More importantly, the ERM band has now reached a point where action to lessen pressure has become unavoidable.

Since the Irish pound is clearly the divergent currency in the band, the onus for such action is on the Irish authorities," NCB said, adding that it believes this will will ultimately result in a reduction in domestic interest rates.

The liklihood that German interest rates will be reduced further, perhaps by as much as 0.5 percent in the next month or so is another source of downward pressure on Irish rates, NCB said in a monthly research note.

It expects three-month money and five-year yields to fall to around five percent in the next six months from 5.75 and 5.5 percent respectively while 10-year yields are seen dropping below six percent.
In other comments, the broker said it expected the Irish economy to grow strongly again this year with real GDP up seven percent and GNP growth close to six percent.

Despite the strength of activity, inflation should remain stable, averaging two percent in 1997, as the appreciation of the Irish pound's trade-weighted index in 1996 and continuing benign domestic cost conditions ensure little risk of deterioration.
